capabilities: Open web apps as panes via customizable iframes
Embed frames in Markdown using a code block syntax
Apply preset configurations for sites like Google Keep and Todoist
Customize frames with custom CSS, ribbon icons, and mobile toggles
disambiguation: Not a window-layout or workspace manager; it embeds external web apps in panes and Markdown embeds.
extras: Mobile support is limited because Obsidian Mobile lacks Electron's permissive iframe behavior; many login-protected sites will not work there, and a per-frame 'Disable on Mobile' toggle exists. Popups open in the system browser by default, which can break external logins unless the Web viewer core plugin is enabled.
intentEvidence: motivating me to turn Obsidian Keep into a more versatile plugin, which is how Custom Frames was born
motivation: The author was motivated to turn the Obsidian Keep plugin into a more versatile plugin, which became Custom Frames.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to keep external web apps visible inside the vault, forcing users to switch to a browser or separate window.
